clue.text: LA boys irresponsibly smuggling instrument? Yes!

indicators.note: to smuggle is to carry something hidden inside, so one piece is tucked within the other
acting irresponsibly means behaving without order or care, so the letters before it are thrown about

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged
a lute is a plucked string instrument

explanation.surface: Some careless Los Angeles lads sneaking an instrument past someone, and the speaker gleefully approving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' with a question mark looks like the definition, but the clue's whole answer is the exclamation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic word of agreement, used as a reply meaning an unreserved yes.

clue.text: Carry away muscle tube

parts.note: ab is short for an abdominal muscle
a duct is a tube or channel in the body

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a tube made of muscle, as in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct someone is to take them off by force, to carry them off illegally.

clue.text: Spaghetti sauce's turned up — that's sweet

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up flips it to read from bottom to top

parts.note: ragù is the meat sauce served on spaghetti, with the s from the possessive

explanation.surface: A cook reports that the pasta sauce has appeared and calls that lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is part of the wordplay, giving the letter that comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is a sweet substance, and 'sweet' can be a noun for a sugary thing; the word also serves as an endearment.

clue.text: This is getting out: actress Grant conceals alternate name (Graunstein, originally)

indicators.note: something that conceals keeps an object hidden inside it

parts.note: Lee Grant is the American film and stage actress
aka means also known as, introducing another name

indicators.note: originally refers to how a word begins, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A gossip item about an actress hiding a former name, which is now coming to light.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee Grant is an American actress who has worked under a name other than her birth name, which gives the surface its scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the act of escaping or seeping out, so it is the process of something getting out.

clue.text: Multi-legged creature amid ultra-creepy arachnids, chiefly!

definitions.text: Multi-legged creature amid ultra-creepy arachnids, chiefly

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece is set inside the rest
creepy suggests crawling and unsettled movement, so the letters squirm into a new order

parts.note: an ant is a six-legged insect
taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: chiefly means mainly, at the head, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of arachnids

explanation.surface: A many-legged beast found among some extremely scary eight-legged animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: the creature sits among very creepy arachnids.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, an eight-legged arachnid that many find creepy.

clue.text: See, the youngest March girl is dirty

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
Amy is the youngest March sister in Little Women

explanation.surface: Look: little Amy from Little Women has got herself muddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Loamy means full of loam, a rich soil, so it is earthy, the soil sense of dirty.

clue.text: Kind of saxophone needed to make unusual tone

indicators.note: the following words are what is needed to make the answer: its letters are already sitting inside them

parts.note: read across the end of unusual and the start of tone

explanation.surface: A musician wonders which type of sax produces a strange sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The alto is the mid-range member of the saxophone family, pitched between soprano and tenor.

clue.text: On the way up, rock band and others surround Orange County laggard

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so these pieces go round another
in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: R.E.M. is the American rock band
OC is the usual short form of Orange County in California
et al. is Latin for and others

explanation.surface: A rising rock group and their entourage gather around a slow resident of Orange County.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer arrives after the others, so is one who lags behind, a straggler.

clue.text: At the opening, oboists refocus freely? Yes!

indicators.note: done freely means without fixed constraints, so the letters move into any order
the opening of a word is its start, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of oboists
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: At a concert's start, do the oboe players adjust their attention as they like? Naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course is an everyday phrase of assent meaning naturally or certainly.

clue.text: Leaving a lousy tip when starting late and cutting short a lunch in London

indicators.note: a word that starts late has lost its opening letter
cutting something short removes its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to stiff a waiter is to leave little or no tip

explanation.surface: A diner arrives late, eats a quick lunch in London and leaves a poor tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiffin, a word from British India, is a light midday meal, so a lunch as said in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is a British and Anglo-Indian name for a light midday meal, so it is a lunch.

clue.text: Follow mother's doctrine

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
ma is an informal word for mother; the possessive just joins the pieces

explanation.surface: An instruction to take up the beliefs one's mother holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a set of principles laid down as unquestionably true, which is what a doctrine is.

clue.text: Rewritten article is sensible

indicators.note: something rewritten has had its material set down again in a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor reports that a reworked piece of journalism now makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like the sentence's verb, but its letters belong in the mix alongside article.
explanation.definitionFit: Being realistic means having a practical, level-headed view of things, a synonym of sensible.

clue.text: Clarinet broken by youths, initially? Yes!

indicators.note: something broken has been smashed apart, so its letters can be put back in any order

parts.note: the letters of the instrument's name, to be rearranged

indicators.note: initially points at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of youths

explanation.surface: Asked whether young people smashed the clarinet, someone confirms it.
explanation.definitionFit: Certainly is a firm word of assent, said in reply to mean yes without doubt.

clue.text: Garment displayed by terrific hunk

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the words that follow, so the answer is read straight out of them

parts.note: read across the end of terrific and the start of hunk

explanation.surface: A handsome man shows off a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A fichu is a small triangular shawl worn round the shoulders and tied at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is an item of clothing, a light neckerchief or shawl, so it is a garment.

clue.text: Penalty? Yes!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sum of money paid as punishment
second meaning: an expression of agreement, as in 'that's all right'

explanation.walkthrough: The question and answer look like a referee being asked about a spot kick, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a monetary punishment and also a reply accepting something, like okay.

clue.text: Dazzled, like an unwilling seaman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: strongly struck with admiration
second meaning: forced into naval service, as press gangs once did

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is pressing in the old naval way: men seized and made to serve at sea against their will.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means filled with admiration and also, historically, forcibly enlisted as a sailor.

clue.text: Mensa ruse changed requirements for access

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A trick for getting into the high-IQ society Mensa means its entry rules had to be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: Mensa is the society for people with high IQs.
explanation.definitionFit: Logging in to an account demands a login name along with a password, so these are things needed to get in.

clue.text: Primitive conversation curtailed after three consecutive letters

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the final letter is removed
after means coming later, so the first piece follows the second

parts.note: three letters in a row of the alphabet, L, M and N, each spelt out as a word
talk is conversation

explanation.surface: Early human chat that broke off after only a few letters had been uttered.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters are not written as letters but as their names, el, em and en.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means basic and fundamental, close to a raw or primal state, so primitive.

clue.text: Sentimentality achieved extra-superficially? Yes!

parts.note: goo is gushing sentimental talk
did is achieved, as in did the job

indicators.note: superficially means only on the surface, so just the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of extra

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that some mush got by only on the surface, then agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Good idea is an enthusiastic reply approving a suggestion, so it works as agreement.

clue.text: Solo interrupting scandalous opera about grand home for children

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so this piece goes inside the other
something scandalous is outrageous and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Han Solo is the Star Wars smuggler
taken as written, to be rearranged
G is short for grand, a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A solo cuts into a shocking opera about a grand house for youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo' is not a musical solo but Han Solo; 'about' just puts the jumbled opera round G before HAN goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is an institution that houses and cares for children without parents.

clue.text: Think highly of spot by a swamp

parts.note: a spot is a short advertisement on TV or radio
a mire is a stretch of bog or swamp

explanation.surface: Someone praises a beauty spot beside a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a place or a mark; here it is an advertising spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to regard them with respect and approval.

clue.text: Returning dealer used connection? Yes!

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters are read from right to left
the answer sits at the join where two neighbouring words connect

parts.note: the end of dealer and the start of used, joined

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a card dealer who came back drew on a contact, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure is a casual word of agreement, meaning certainly or of course.

clue.text: Exploded, 23 is a weapon

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so its letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 23 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that a blown-up fantasy can be used as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to the answer of 23 across, whose letters join IS in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a pistol or other weapon carried at the side or in a belt.

clue.text: Go around near spas, running amok…

parts.note: by means near, as in standing by

indicators.note: running amok means rushing wildly out of control, so the letters break formation

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Visitors circling close to health resorts and going wild.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to avoid it by taking a route round it, so to circumvent.

clue.text: Imagine rapping doctor in the morning

parts.note: Dr Dre is the hip-hop producer and rapper
a.m. marks a time before noon

explanation.surface: Someone pictures a physician giving a rap performance before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' wants to be DR, but the 'rapping doctor' is Dr Dre, giving DRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream is to picture something in the mind, a synonym of imagine as a verb.

clue.text: Love a tonality to be sufficient clue? Yes!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a key is the tonality a piece of music is written in
to do is to be enough, as in 'that will do'
a key is a clue to solving something

explanation.surface: A musician wonders whether affection and a home key are enough of a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Okey-dokey is a jokey, informal form of okay, said to mean yes or all right.

clue.text: …in a peculiar fashion — or did I lay this way?

indicators.note: this way points back to the definition's manner, telling you to keep the odd-numbered letters of the words before it

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of these words

explanation.surface: A puzzled speaker wonders whether they arranged things in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 22 down, whose ellipsis carries the running-amok scene over. The answer word describes its own method: read the letters the way it says.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddly means strangely or unusually, which is acting in a peculiar fashion.

clue.text: Railroad company in the ascendant becomes timeless moral force

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means moving upwards, so the letters read from the bottom
timeless means without time, and time is abbreviated to one letter that is dropped

parts.note: Amtrak is the US national passenger rail company

explanation.surface: A rail firm on the rise turns into an eternal ethical power.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist belief, karma is the force by which one's deeds determine one's future fate.

clue.text: Something round and bloody — it is a blemish

parts.note: a disc is a flat circular object
red is the colour of blood
taken as written

explanation.surface: A round, blood-coloured spot is described as a mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A discredit is a stain on one's reputation, a figurative blemish or source of disgrace.

clue.text: A court proceeding reduced in courts

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a trial is a hearing in a court of law

explanation.surface: A legal case gets shortened when heard in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courts' in the surface is the legal sense, but the definition means open courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards in a building, so courts in the architectural sense.

clue.text: Support a Verdi opera

parts.note: to aid is to support or help
taken as written

explanation.surface: An appeal to back a particular work by Verdi.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is the famous Verdi opera set in ancient Egypt, an example of his works.

clue.text: Redesign many labels? Yes!

indicators.note: to redesign is to plan something over in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to rework a whole set of product tags and gets an eager go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: By all means is a courteous phrase granting permission, a polite form of certainly.
